newsitem.title: USA: Johnson sworn in as Jackson, Miss. first black mayor.
newsitem.headline: Johnson sworn in as Jackson, Miss. first black mayor.

text.p: Harvey Johnson became the first black mayor of Jackson on Monday during a ceremony that contrasted the painful memories of segregation with modern-day optimism about the prospects for racial unity.

Standing on the white-columned porch of a city hall building erected by African slaves, the 50-year-old Democrat took the oath of office as a racially mixed crowd of more than a thousand people stood by to witness the historic event.

"I am looking to the future, but I cannot forget whence we came. Lockstep, hand in hand, young and old, black and white, rich and poor ... we will go forward together," Johnson proclaimed amid calls of "Amen!" from onlookers.

The new mayor said his arrival in office represented the dream of slain civil rights leader Medgar Evers, who was gunned down outside his Jackson home in 1963, while serving as Mississippi field secretary for the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People.
No one was convicted for the murder until 1994, when avowed white supremacist Byron De La Beckwith was tried for a third time and found guilty by a mixed-race jury.
"Lord, just think how far we've come," Johnson told the cheering crowd. "This very moment represents Medgar Evers' dream come true!"

Among the crowd of onlookers, many of whom sought relief from the noon-day heat in the shade of nearby magnolia trees, the only protest came from a lone white-supremacist who held a hand-printed sign which read: "No good ever comes from the slaves taking over the plantation."

Johnson, an urban planner, forged a coalition of black and white voters to defeat two-term Mayor Kane Ditto in the Democratic Party primary May 8. He went on to defeat Republican businesswoman Charlotte Reeves in the general election June 3.
About 60 percent of Jackson's 197,000 inhabitants are black.
